We cut p99 latency of our Postgres-backed queue from 900 ms to 40 ms. The fix: SKIP LOCKED plus a partial index on (status, run_at). Write-up with the query plans and the benchmark script in the thread.

New paper compares GRPO and PPO on math reasoning at 1.5B and 7B. Same compute budget, 3 seeds each. GRPO wins at 1.5B, the gap closes at 7B, and both collapse without a KL term. Tables and code linked.
Three finger-strength protocols compared over 8 weeks with 24 climbers: max hangs gained 11%, repeaters 7%, no-hangs 9% with half the skin wear. Data sheet and the session plans are public.
TIL: content-visibility: auto on long lists cut our initial render from 1.8 s to 0.6 s on a mid-range Android. Caveat: you need contain-intrinsic-size or the scrollbar jumps. Repro repo in replies.
Postmortem: a single misconfigured retry policy turned a 2-minute DNS blip into a 40-minute outage. Timeline, the exact config diff, and the three guardrails we added afterwards.
Benchmark: Parquet with ZSTD level 3 gave the best size/speed trade-off on our 2 TB event table, 38% smaller than Snappy with 6% slower scans. Full matrix of codecs and row-group sizes attached.
We're open-sourcing our RL infrastructure: 8,192 concurrent sandboxes, ~1.3M rollouts in 7 days. Code, configs and the training report are on GitHub.
We're hiring two research engineers for our post-training team, remote within EU time zones. You'd own RL environments and evals. Details and salary range in the link.

I spent a week measuring how often our eval judge disagrees with itself. Same inputs, temperature 0: 4% of verdicts flip between runs. Writeup on why, and the fix (majority of 3) that brought it to 0.3%.
Security advisory: versions 2.3.0 to 2.3.4 of the library leak request headers into debug logs. Upgrade to 2.3.5; if you can't, set LOG_LEVEL=info. CVE pending.
Our city opened a new protected bike lane on Main Street this week. Early counts: 1,800 riders a day, up from 600, and no change in car travel times so far.

After 10 years of running a small bakery, here are the numbers: rent is 18% of revenue, flour went up 40% since 2022, and the most profitable item is the one I almost dropped. Thread on what I'd do differently.
Strongly disagree with the take that code review is obsolete. In our team, review caught 3 of the 5 production incidents we would have had last quarter. Here's what those reviews looked like.
Hot take, but with numbers: our 'AI-written' PRs had 2x more revert commits than human ones over 6 months (412 PRs). Breakdown by repo and by type of change below.

Short and sweet: if your Docker builds are slow, put COPY package*.json and npm ci before COPY . — the dependency layer stays cached. Cut ours from 6 min to 40 s.
